title: Substitute
text: Let $$x=sin(\theta)$$. Then the integral becomes the integral of $$cos^4\left(\theta\right)$$ with respect to θ.

title: Integrate and convert back
text: Using the power-reducing formula twice, the integral is $$\frac{3}{8} \theta$$ plus $$\frac{1}{4} sin\left(2\theta\right)$$ plus $$\frac{1}{32} sin\left(4\theta\right)$$. Then write everything in terms of $$x$$.
